page: Amazon Web Services r6i.2xlarge is an x86_64 memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. The system features an Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at a base or all-core frequency of up to 3.5 GHz. Hardware resources include 4 dedicated physical cores supporting 2 threads per core, yielding 8 vCPUs. CPU cache architecture includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 54 MB L3 cache. Supported instruction set extensions include AVX, AVX-512 (AVX512F and AVX512_VNNI), AES, VAES, SHA-NI, and BMI2, which assist in cryptographic and vectorized calculations.

Memory capacity is configured at 64.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, providing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio (8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU). In benchmark testing, the memory subsystem achieved an uncached large-block read bandwidth of 58.24 GB/sec and a write bandwidth of 42.08 GB/sec, alongside a cached small-block read rate of 413.39 GB/sec. The instance does not include integrated local NVMe storage or dedicated GPUs, requiring network-attached storage via Amazon EBS. Network connectivity provides a baseline bandwidth of 3 Gbps without complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations position the r6i.2xlarge solidly within average percentiles across general compute and memory workflows. The instance recorded a Geekbench multi-core score of 6046.0 and a single-core score of 1628.0, with stress-ng recording 7719.55 multi-core points. In-memory and caching operations show consistent throughput, with Redis recording 7.96 million SET operations per second and web serving delivering 11.9 GB/sec throughput. However, memory performance in PassMark (1819.56) and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (31.9 GB/sec) scored in the lower percentiles. CPU-bound LLM inference on a 7B model delivered 16.14 prompt tokens per second and 7.53 generation tokens per second.

With its 8:1 memory configuration, the r6i.2xlarge is well-aligned for memory-intensive enterprise tasks such as distributed in-memory caches, relational database systems, real-time data analytics, and general memory-bound backend services. For compute-heavy or disk-bound jobs, the absence of local ephemeral storage and the standard core count may present throughput tradeoffs that necessitate pairing with provisioned network storage.
description: Amazon Web Services r6i.2xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz on the AWS Nitro System. Configured on the x86_64 architecture, it delivers 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores and integrates 64.0 GB of DDR4 memory at 3 GHz, producing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. The instance features AVX-512 vector acceleration, a 54 MB L3 cache, and a 3 Gbps baseline network interface. It lacks bundled local storage and discrete GPUs, relying on Amazon EBS for persistent storage. Benchmark testing reveals solid middle-tier performance, producing 7.96 million Redis SET operations per second, a Geekbench multi-core score of 6046.0, and 58.24 GB/sec uncached read bandwidth. The r6i.2xlarge is structured for memory-dense enterprise workloads, including in-memory key-value caching, relational databases, and data processing.
